They settled in Paterson, New Jersey, the Silk City.
In 1791 Alexander Hamilton’s Society for Establishing Useful Manufactures chose the Great Falls of the Passaic to
power a planned industrial town, and by the late 1800s Paterson made more silk than any other city in America,
its mills filled by one wave of immigrants after another.
By the 1950s most of the silk mills had closed, but the city still had textile mills and garment shops,
and they took on newcomers. Zinaida worked as a seamstress for Style Sportswear in Paterson,
and she died at Lincoln Park, New Jersey, in 2008.
